claims.claim: C1: fix outdated permitting and licensing systems
claims.excerpt: I’ll focus on cutting red tape and streamlining permitting processes to support local businesses
claims.note: Same Daily Herald page also: 'Inefficient processes for permits and licensing frustrate both residents and local businesses.' Also April 2026 Herald interview on streamlining permits.

claims.claim: C2: update Master Plan; reverse declining sales tax revenue with neighborhood-focused growth
claims.excerpt: I’ll lead a much-needed update to the city’s master plan
claims.note: Same page: 'Our sales tax revenue has been steadily declining, putting pressure on our city’s budget.' Campaign site /taxes page: 'change the zoning to allow for neighborhood friendly retail, restaurants, and services.' (https://www.marshajudkins.com/taxes) Ad and sources agree.

claims.excerpt: I’ll also work with stakeholders to revitalize downtown and address urgent infrastructure needs.
claims.note: Campaign site /taxes page: 'We need a vision and plan for Downtown' (more concrete: Rooftop Concert Series, First Friday Art Stroll, Center Street planning).

SB 2001 = 2019 Third Special Session tax bill (House passed 43-27). KSL says only that 'Some Republican lawmakers joined Democrats in the House and Senate in voting against SB2001'; no names. le.utah.gov static page 404, vote page returned SQL error. Judkins campaign site /taxes does not mention SB 2001. Roll call not reachable; not verified.

claims.claim: C5: advocate for local control, limited government, less regulation
claims.excerpt: I will get things done without growing government.
claims.note: Closest match is limited government. No 'local control' phrase found in sources. Campaign site: 'Government exists to serve the people—to make life easier, not more complicated.' (https://www.marshajudkins.com/role-of-city-government). Red-tape cutting appears under C1.

people.name: Katrice MacKay
sources_checked: searches: MacKay + app/311/Slate Canyon/zoning (3), campaign website (1)

claims.claim: C1: zoning should reflect each neighborhood's own concerns; pledge to listen to every neighborhood
claims.excerpt: I’ve listened, asked questions and worked to make sure your voice is heard.
claims.note: Zoning mentioned only as enforcement: 'things like property maintenance, zoning and neighborhood standards.' Not the same position as neighborhood-specific zoning. Ad is more specific.

claims.claim: C2: keep parks beautiful and well maintained
claims.excerpt: I’ll continue to fight for parks and open space.
claims.note: Same answer: 'Everyone deserves access to the outdoors — now and in the future.' Supports parks, not specifically maintenance.

claims.claim: C3: smartphone app / 311 to communicate with the city
claims.note: Not in Herald questionnaire. Searches for MacKay + app/311 found nothing. No campaign site found. Provo directory page blocked (403).

claims.claim: C4: stated position on future of Slate Canyon (video)
claims.note: Slate Canyon appears in the Herald Q&A only in another candidate's answers (Jeff Whitlock, opposing a waterpark). No MacKay position found in news or minutes reached. Council minutes not checked individually.

claims.claim: C1: no tax increases; county should live within its means
claims.excerpt: government must live within its means just like families do.
claims.note: Same site: 'opposing excessive tax increases'. Lehi Free Press (Mar 2026) says he 'strongly believes that tax increases must be put on the ballot for citizens to decide' - a vote-on-ballot position, slightly different from flat no-increase.

claims.excerpt: I will not raise my salary. I want to decrease it.
claims.note: Lehi Free Press Mar 2026: he promises to 'roll back those pay increases' and cut travel budgets from $20,000 to $10,000. Sources go further than the ad (rollback).

claims.claim: C3: oppose bigger county budgets and higher fees
claims.note: Lehi Free Press Mar 2026: wants to 'drive operational costs down across the board.' Budget-cutting found; no source mentions fees (Lehi Free Press and campaign site both silent on fees).
